chapter: Dancers, Newton, Chu Berry and the Cab Calloway band
title: Frankie Newton as friend and intellectual
summary: Newton's long talks at the Rhythm Club, his death and his Village life.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Why don't we talk about Frankie Newton, back to him. You did some records with him in '37.
'37, that's right.
And '39.
I knew Frankie very well and he used to come by, you know, the Rhythm Club, the Band Box, in the afternoons we used to have long sessions, talk sessions, you know, sit

around and talk, and then he used to call me on his dates, record dates, and I enjoyed them, and our relationship was very nice, it was a true relationship, Frankie and I, we liked each other. Talk about music together, you know, different things, and I did several recording dates with him.
He was said to be a very intellectual person.
Yeah.
Very well read.

Yeah, yeah, he was. Frankie, a nice looking man, too, and very intelligent. Sit around and really talk. He was very well versed on current events, everything. I enjoyed just sitting around talking with Frankie. He was well liked, musicians.
Why do you think he never made more of a success than he did?
I don't know, he was about to make it just before he died. I don't know.
Which was when? Let me just check that quickly. 1954.
Was that when he died?
Yeah.
'54, was it that late?
Yeah. It said last years of his life did little regular playing, lived in Greenwich Village, devoting considerable time to painting and politics.
Yeah, yeah.
Did you ever talk about those things with him?
No, politics and things like that, no. I went down to his pad there in Greenwich Village, Bohemian style, you know.
Yeah, that was the era.
Yeah.
Early '50s.
Yeah. We had some wonderful little times together, just sitting around chatting, talking, playing records, things like that.
